conversation.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, doctor, I've been feeling really tired lately — not like the usual kind of tired, but more like my energy is just completely drained all the time. And then I noticed these little lumps on the sides of my neck too. It's been making me a bit anxious, to be honest.
When did you first notice the neck lumps, and how long have you had them?
I first felt the lumps a few months ago, but I thought it was just because I'd been sleeping on my pillow wrong or something. But they haven't gone away, so now I'm really worried about it.
Have you had any other symptoms, such as fevers, night sweats, weight loss, or sore throat?

Not really, doctor. Aside from the fatigue and the lumps in my neck, I've been pretty much feeling normal. No fevers, no sore throats, and I haven't lost any weight that I'm aware of. But I have to admit, my appetite has been a bit off lately too.
Have you had these neck lumps examined before, and do you have any known medical conditions?

No, I haven't had them checked out yet because I didn't think much of it at first. But now that they're still there, I'm definitely worried. As for medical conditions, I've been struggling with high blood pressure for a few years now, but that's about it.
What blood pressure medication are you currently taking, and have you had any blood tests or imaging done recently?

I'm on some sort of pill that the doctor gave me to help with my blood pressure. I can't remember the name right now, but I've been taking it as directed. As for blood tests or imaging, I don't think I've had either recently — at least not since my last checkup a few months ago.
When was your last blood pressure checkup, and have you been able to feel any tenderness or changes in size of the neck lumps?

I can't remember exactly when it was, but I think it was around the same time as my last doctor's appointment — a few months ago. And as for the lumps, they don't really hurt or anything like that, but they do seem to be growing in size, which is making me even more worried.
Who noticed the lumps are growing — you, or someone else? And when was the last time you saw your primary care doctor specifically for your blood pressure?

It's mostly just me who has noticed the lumps getting bigger. I haven't told anyone else about it yet because I didn't want to worry them unnecessarily. As for my blood pressure, I think the last time I saw my doctor specifically for it was around three months ago. But like I said earlier, I'm not sure when exactly that was.
Have you noticed any difficulty swallowing, breathing, or changes in your voice when you talk?

No, doctor, nothing like that. I can still swallow just fine and my breathing hasn't changed at all. And as far as my voice goes, it sounds the same to me. But then again, I'm not a professional singer or anything, so maybe I wouldn't notice if something was off.
Are you taking any other medications, including over-the-counter drugs, vitamins, or supplements?

No, doctor, I'm not on any other medications besides the blood pressure pill. And as far as vitamins and supplements go, I take a multivitamin every day just to make sure I'm getting all my nutrients, but that's about it.
Have you had any recent infections or illnesses, such as colds, sore throats, or flu, in the past few months?

No, doctor, I haven't had anything like that recently. I've been trying to stay healthy and avoid getting sick by washing my hands a lot and keeping my distance from people who are coughing or sneezing. But other than that, I can't think of any recent illnesses or infections.
Do you have any family history of cancer or other chronic conditions, and are you worried that the lumps might be cancerous?

Yes, doctor, there is a family history of breast cancer on my mother's side, but I'm not sure about any other types of cancer. And to be honest, ever since I found out about these lumps, I've been really scared and worried that they could be something serious like cancer.
Given your family history of breast cancer, have you had any breast screening or mammograms? And have you noticed any lumps or swelling anywhere else in your body?

I haven't had a mammogram yet because I'm not at the age where they typically recommend them. But as far as lumps and swelling go, besides these neck lumps, I can't think of anything else that's out of the ordinary.
How old are you, and have you had any recent dental work or infections in your mouth or throat?

I'm 63 years old, doctor. And as far as dental work or infections go, I went to the dentist a few months ago for my regular cleaning and checkup, but they didn't find anything wrong. And since then, I haven't had any issues with my teeth or gums that I can think of.
What is the name of your blood pressure medication, and have you had any contact with pesticides, chemicals, or hazardous materials in your work or home environment?

I'm not sure what the name of my blood pressure medication is — it's been a few months since I was prescribed it. And as for exposure to chemicals or hazardous materials, I don't think there's anything like that in my work or home environment. I work mostly with computers and office supplies, so I wouldn't be handling anything dangerous like that.
Have you traveled recently, either domestically or internationally? And do you smoke or have a history of smoking?

I haven't traveled anywhere out of state in the past few months, doctor. But I did go on vacation to visit my family last year, which was about an hour's flight away. As for smoking, I quit smoking almost 10 years ago, so I don't smoke at all anymore.
Have you experienced any night sweats or unexplained itching in the past few months?

Aside from the occasional night sweat that I mentioned earlier, which I think might be related to my blood pressure medication, I haven't had any unexplained itching recently. But then again, it's hard for me to keep track of everything, so there could be other things going on that I'm not aware of.
Is your blood pressure currently well-controlled, and have you noticed any lumps or swelling in your armpits or groin area?

I'm not sure if my blood pressure is well-controlled or not — like I said earlier, I can't remember the last time I had it checked. And as far as lumps or swelling goes, I haven't noticed anything out of the ordinary in those areas, but then again, I don't know what's considered normal for me at this point.
Do you have any other chronic conditions such as diabetes, heart disease, or kidney disease? And when you say your energy is completely drained, what activities are you finding most difficult to do?

No, doctor, I don't have any other chronic conditions besides the high blood pressure. As for my energy levels, even simple tasks like doing the dishes or taking a short walk can leave me feeling exhausted and drained. And then when I try to sleep at night, it's like I'm running on fumes — I just can't seem to get enough rest.
Has this fatigue affected your ability to work or do your daily activities, and have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight?

Yes, doctor, the fatigue has definitely affected my ability to work and do my daily activities. I'm finding that even though I'm trying to maintain my usual routine, it's getting harder and harder to keep up with everything. And as for my appetite and weight, like I mentioned earlier, I've noticed that my appetite has been a bit off lately, but I don't think I've lost any significant amount of weight.
What do you do for work, and have you had a complete blood count or other blood tests done recently to check for anemia or other abnormalities?
